clue.text: Peg's right perhaps, for the borough

parts.note: a golf peg is a tee, here with its possessive s
right is one example of a side, as in the right-hand side

explanation.surface: Someone named Peg is perhaps right about the merits of a local borough.
explanation.walkthrough: Peg looks like a woman's name but is the golf tee. TEESSIDE is an area of north-east England around the River Tees, including Middlesbrough.
explanation.definitionFit: Teesside was the name of a county borough in north-east England, a local government district.

clue.text: Square prime minister? Not quite — it's only gossip

parts.note: a T-square is a drawing tool, giving the letter T

indicators.note: not quite means the name stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: Clement Attlee was the British prime minister from 1945 to 1951

explanation.surface: An honest prime minister is being discussed, though it is only idle talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' removes the final E from ATTLEE, the post-war Labour prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To tattle is to chatter idly or tell tales, an idle-talk synonym.

clue.text: I orally gave permission for the opening

indicators.note: orally means spoken, so the letter is replaced by a word with the same pronunciation

parts.note: the pronoun I
let is past tense of allow, gave permission

explanation.surface: Someone says they allowed the launch to go ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small hole for a lace or cord, a type of opening.

clue.text: Additional price on French demand

parts.note: sur is the French word for on
a charge is a demand for payment

explanation.surface: Extra charges on French goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge is an extra fee added to the normal cost.

clue.text: After a party, bad boys do make a survey of the land

indicators.note: after puts the anagram following the party word

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are damaged and rearranged

explanation.surface: Following a party, naughty boys go out and carry out a land survey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' looks like it describes the boys, but it is the anagram signal for the three words that follow it. 'After' puts the scrambled words behind the party.
explanation.definitionFit: The Domesday Book of 1086 recorded William the Conqueror's survey of England's landholdings.

clue.text: Cupid's beloved soul

explanation.surface: Cupid's beloved soul, a romantic phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the mortal girl loved by Cupid (Eros) bears this name, and in Greek the word also means the spirit or mind.

clue.text: Sails woven by the Weaver of Raveloe

indicators.note: woven suggests strands interlaced, so the letters of sails are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sails made by a weaver in a village.
explanation.walkthrough: Raveloe is the village in George Eliot's novel Silas Marner, whose title character is a weaver.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot's linen-weaver hero of Raveloe is named Silas Marner.

clue.text: Study representations from hands over here

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
signs are symbols that represent things

explanation.surface: Someone examines depictions passed across to them.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is an old word for studying a text closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To consign goods is to deliver or entrust them to someone, giving them up.

clue.text: Apply current to make a change in 23, note

indicators.note: make a change says the letters of the following words are altered in order

parts.note: the answer to 23 across, the cloth
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Instructions to electrify something and alter cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: '23' points to the answer at 23 across, the cloth. 'make a change' scrambles the cloth together with the word in, and the musical note goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To energise a circuit is to switch power through it, supplying electricity.

clue.text: Article and book about state propositions

clue.text: Look — first stage of guided weapon!

indicators.note: the first stage of a word is its opening letter, taken here from guided

parts.note: a lance is a long spear, a weapon of mounted knights

explanation.surface: An excited cry to watch the opening phase of a guided missile launch.
explanation.definitionFit: A glance is a brief look, a synonym.

clue.text: Have a hit after long stoppage

indicators.note: after puts the hitting word following the yearning word

parts.note: to long for something is to hunger for it
to strike is to hit

explanation.surface: A batsman finally connects after a long wait in play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective for the stoppage but is the verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunger strike is a protest in which a person stops eating, a refusal of food.

clue.text: Worm concealed in a little echinoid

indicators.note: concealed in says the letters sit within the run of words little echinoid

explanation.surface: A parasite is found hiding inside a small sea urchin.
explanation.walkthrough: An echinoid is a sea urchin; the answer runs across the end of little and the start of echinoid.
explanation.definitionFit: The leech is an annelid, a segmented worm that sucks blood.

clue.text: Putting down a drink — gin maybe

parts.note: squash is a British fruit cordial diluted with water, a soft drink

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word gin could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Someone downs a drink, possibly gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting down' sounds like setting a drink on the table, but it means suppressing. 'maybe' scrambles GIN into ING. Squash in Britain is a fruit concentrate you dilute with water.
explanation.definitionFit: Squashing a rebellion or an objection is suppressing it, the same as putting it down.

clue.text: Plans made for mountain folk to enter the faculty

indicators.note: to enter says one group of letters goes into the middle of another

parts.note: the arts are a university faculty
a mountain range, a chain of peaks
folk taken as people in general, men

explanation.surface: Arrangements are made for highlanders to join a university department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mountain folk' looks like one idea, highlanders, but it splits into two pieces. 'to enter' sends both of them into the faculty word, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrangements are preparations or schemes worked out in advance, synonyms of plans.

clue.text: Great confusion at Rommel's failure

indicators.note: failure suggests something breaking down, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Chaos follows the German general Rommel's defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of Rommel's is used as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a violent whirlpool, and figuratively a state of turmoil.

clue.text: Case of sailor overdue about four

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: about says the late word wraps around the number

parts.note: late means overdue
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A legal case about a sailor who is overdue on four counts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a lawsuit but it is a grammatical case. 'about' wraps the overdue word around the Roman four.
explanation.definitionFit: The ablative is a grammatical case in Latin.

clue.text: Escalation of the striker's position

explanation.surface: A batsman's place at the wicket leads to escalation.
explanation.definitionFit: An increase is an escalation; and in cricket the batsman facing, the striker, stands in the crease, the line marked at the wicket.

clue.text: The source of a heated retort?

definitions.text: The source of a heated retort?

parts.words: The source of a heated retort
parts.note: a heated retort sounds like an angry reply, but a retort is also a glass vessel heated in a chemistry laboratory by a gas flame

explanation.surface: Asking what provoked an angry reply.
explanation.definitionFit: This gas appliance is the standard laboratory flame used to heat flasks and retorts.

clue.text: Clever economist

explanation.surface: A smart economist.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright means intelligent; and John Bright was the Victorian free-trade campaigner and political economist.

clue.text: Does he sing, say, for money?

indicators.note: say means the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a tenor is a male singer

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man will sing for payment.
explanation.walkthrough: A TENNER is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenner is a ten-pound note, an amount of cash.

clue.text: Pointer to the origin of American plant

parts.note: an arrow is a sign that points the way
a root is the origin or source of something

explanation.surface: A sign directing visitors to where an American plant came from.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrowroot is a tropical American plant whose rhizome yields an edible starch.

clue.text: Thrash wife well

parts.note: hale means healthy, well

explanation.surface: Someone beats their wife thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: To whale is an old informal verb meaning to beat or thrash.

clue.text: Russian material

explanation.surface: Fabric from Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a typical Russian man's first name, and it is also a hard-wearing twilled woollen cloth.

clue.text: Book is first class, having a horrendous beginning

parts.note: taken as written
A1 means first class, written with the figure 1 read as the letter I
taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of horrendous is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A first-rate book that nonetheless opens in a horrible way.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is the old Lloyd's Register mark for first class, used in crosswords as AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaiah is a prophetic book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: In Tring one revels — it's the air mostly

indicators.note: revels suggests riotous merrymaking, so the letters of the words are thrown about

explanation.surface: In a small English town someone celebrates, and the whole atmosphere is festive.
explanation.walkthrough: Tring is a small market town in Hertfordshire; 'revels' rearranges TRINGONE.
explanation.definitionFit: This gas makes up roughly four fifths of the atmosphere, so the air is mostly made of it.

clue.text: Team's coffee time

explanation.surface: A sports side takes its mid-morning coffee break.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has this many players; and in Britain a mid-morning coffee break, elevenses, is taken at that hour of the morning.

clue.text: Driver with examiner going about a mile

indicators.note: going about says the examiner's word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a tester is one who examines or tries something out
taken as written

explanation.surface: A driver accompanied by a driving examiner covers about a mile.
explanation.definitionFit: A teamster is a driver, originally of a team of horses, now especially of a truck in the US.
